page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores across 2 threads per core) derived from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes x86_64 vector and matrix execution instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, accompanied by hardware cryptographic features like AES and VAES. It provides 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU, paired with 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. It contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU throughput alongside competitive memory performance. The stress-ng single-core score of 3,789.09 and single-threaded gzip compression at 40.71 GB/sec place the instance in the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded processing scores remain solid, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 58,651.77 and PassMark memory score of 2,886.79. Data decompression with bzip3 achieved 17.64 GB/sec on a single thread and 207.89 GB/sec in multi-threaded testing. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 102.21 GB/sec with write throughput reaching 67.4 GB/sec.

CPU-based machine learning inference metrics indicate distinct capability thresholds based on parameter scale. Small model (135M) prompt processing and generation deliver strong-to-top-tier performance, achieving 3,681.85 tokens/sec and 435.32 tokens/sec respectively. Performance normalizes to average tiers when running medium 7B models (24.51 tokens/sec generation) and drops to 2.45 tokens/sec on large 70B models, illustrating the CPU compute limitations for large parameter inference despite the expansive 512.0 GB memory footprint.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the constrained core count lowers potential core-based database software licensing overhead while retaining the massive 512.0 GB memory pool and fast 3,780 GB NVMe local disk. The primary trade-off is reduced aggregate parallel compute relative to a full 64-vCPU instance. As such, the E64-32ads_v7 is suitable for high-memory, disk-intensive workloads, including relational database management systems, in-memory caches such as Redis, analytical batch operations, and large-footprint ETL data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor at 4.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:16 core-to-memory ratio, it supplies 512.0 GB of RAM alongside 3,780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. The instance excels in single-threaded operations, achieving top-tier stress-ng single-core marks (3,789.09) and fast gzip compression (40.71 GB/sec), coupled with strong PassMark CPU performance (58,651.77). Memory throughput registers 102.21 GB/sec for uncached reads. Its resource allocation profile lowers per-core licensing expenses while maintaining high memory and local storage capacities. This architecture is well suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, enterprise data processing, and large ETL workflows.
